acceptance: Every income, contra-income and expense account in the system chart (src/domains/books/system-chart.json) carries a Schedule C line, proven by tests/schedule-c-mapping.test.ts; owner-added or unmapped accounts fall back to line 27a (Other expenses) listed by name, never dropped.

The accountant packet for fed.income.schedule_c is prepared from the posted books for the filing's tax year: year totals by Schedule C line, gross receipts tied to the 1099-K reconciliation, the 4562 and 4797 worksheets and the home-office note when the facts say a home office is used; the packet downloads as CSV and as a generated PDF from the approved filing only.

The 4562 worksheet is built from BookAsset records and their latest tax evidence (cost, placed-in-service date, Section 179, bonus and allowed depreciation) with the dated us.section179 and us.bonus_depreciation rule values shown for the year; assets without tax evidence are listed as needing CPA review, never given invented numbers. The 4797 worksheet is built from the year's retired-appliance sales through the existing Section 1245 estimate (src/domains/sales/retired-sale-tax.ts). Both worksheets are marked 'Estimate — your CPA confirms'.

Quarterly estimates (fed.estimated_tax and co.income.dr0104ep) use the safe-harbor method from the prior year's tax facts the owner enters once per year (TaxYearFacts): required annual payment 100% of last year's tax, 110% when last year's federal AGI is over $150,000, one quarter of that per payment. Colorado uses the same prior-year safe harbor, confirmed against the official 2026 DR 0104EP instructions (100%/110% of the preceding year's net Colorado tax; the 70%-of-actual alternative is not computed and the Decisions question records that). A year with no prior-year facts produces no number — the filing says to enter an estimate from the CPA.

Filled vouchers: the federal voucher comes from the vendored 1040-ES booklet through the existing fillEstimatedTaxVoucher; the Colorado voucher is filled from the official DR 0104EP 2026 PDF vendored from tax.colorado.gov and pinned in the forms manifest (SHA-256 2b4e33fe2bdc4f5e3b324687f11ef7a0b22698673341a7a8b07764203946b12c, fillable voucher on page index 4). The voucher identity (owner name and SSN) is typed at download time and used only to fill that PDF — never stored, logged or audited. The filing page links IRS Direct Pay and Colorado Revenue Online; the app never pays.

The 1099-K tie-out reads the stored StripeBalanceTransaction rows by month (gross charges, fees, refunds, disputes) and compares the year's gross with the 1099-K amount the owner typed from Stripe's form (TaxYearFacts.form1099KGrossCents), showing the difference in the packet. No live Stripe call is made by the tie-out.

TXF export is omitted on purpose: the spec allows building it only after confirming the format spec from an official or vendor source, and no authoritative TXF 042 specification could be confirmed (only secondary summaries; the format is being superseded by FDX). The packet CSV stays. Recorded here and on the card as the packet drift for this item.

Tests named by the work index pass: tests/schedule-c-mapping.test.ts, tests/estimated-tax.test.ts, tests/1099k-tieout.test.ts, plus tests/income-tax-integration.test.ts for the books-based preparation; ci green; every review comment read.
invariants: Estimates are always labelled estimates; no number is invented — a missing prior-year tax fact or missing asset tax evidence yields words ('ask your CPA', 'CPA review needed'), never a fabricated amount.

Nothing is filed and nothing is paid by the app: CMP-2 prepares packets, worksheets and vouchers inside the CMP-1 prepare → approve flow (preparedHash binding), and paying happens only through the IRS and Colorado payment links.
The owner's personal SSN for a voucher is handled like the CMP-1/CMP-3 secrets: typed at download time, used only inside that request's PDF fill, never stored, logged or audited.
Money stays integer cents; times are stored UTC and shown America/Denver; writes lock the row first and re-check the actor inside the transaction.

Schedule C totals come from the posted journal lines of the filing's tax year, the same books the year-end package reads; the mapping never guesses silently — unmapped accounts land on line 27a by name.
next: Full tests, CI, review, merge; then Lane 5's remaining compliance work per MASTER-ROADMAP (CMP-4 next in the compliance spec order). CMP-2 merging also unblocks Lane 4's TAXBEN-1.
outcome: Income tax season works end to end: every books account maps to a Schedule C line; the app prepares the year's accountant packet (Schedule C totals tied to the 1099-K, 4562 and 4797 worksheets marked as CPA-confirm estimates, home-office note) as CSV and PDF under the owner's approval; quarterly federal and Colorado estimates are computed by the safe-harbor method from last year's entered tax (or honestly refuse when there is no prior year), with filled 1040-ES and DR 0104EP vouchers and payment links — the app never pays and never invents a number.
